feedback.problem: A $2\times 3$ matrix $A$ maps the unit sphere ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{3}$ onto an ellipse in ${R}^{2}.$ Given that the eigenvalues of ${A}^{T}A$ are $5,$ $3,$ and $0,$ find the length of the ellipse's semi-major axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
The matrix $A$ maps the unit sphere ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{3}$ onto the ellipse ${Ax\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ in ${R}^{2}.$

First, let's re-write the squared distance from the origin to the point $Ax$ on our ellipse, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖Ax{‖}^{2} & =(Ax)^{T}(Ax) \\  & =({x}^{T}\,{A}^{T})(Ax) \\  & ={x}^{T}\,({A}^{T}\,A)x,\end{aligned}
$$

  

where ${x}^{T}({A}^{T}A)x$ is the quadratic form with the matrix ${A}^{T}A.$ 

The maximum value of this quadratic form, when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of the matrix ${A}^{T}A.$

Since the largest eigenvalue of ${A}^{T}A$ is $5,$ we obtain

$$
{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax{‖}^{2}}=5\,⟹\,{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax‖}=\sqrt{5}.
$$

 

Therefore, the semi-major axis of our ellipse is $\sqrt{5}.$
